requirement:
Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
rationale:
The marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.definitions.inputs`. I did not read implementation source, because the tests' assertions were enough to judge each clause.

**Definition form with exactly `definition` and `text`**
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked]` adds an `unexpected` field to a definition input and asserts an "unexpected field" error.
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required]` removes `text`, sets it to `[]`, and sets it to a plain string. Each case asserts an error from `evidence/rules.ready.json` that mentions `text`.

**`definition` must identify one named definition**
- The same test adds definition inputs naming a requirement (`rules.ready`) and an example (`rules.case`). It asserts a "no matching named definition" error for each.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configuration_and_dependency_failures_do_not_stop_later_checks]` records `rules.gone`, which does not exist. It asserts the `inputs[0]` error for `rules.gone` reads "no matching named definition".
- `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` deletes `md/glossary.md` and asserts the missing-definition error names `glossary.a`.

**`text` is the complete raw fenced declaration**
- The `declaration` and `definition` helpers in `tests/definitions.rs` build the expected text from the source file. It runs from the `:::{definition} …` fence line through the closing `:::`, so it includes the phrase option and the body.
- Validation passes only when the recorded text equals that full declaration.
- Changing the `:phrase:` line and changing body lines both trigger "input text changed". This shows the phrase option and body are part of the snapshot.

**Reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition with a compact diff**
- `cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` changes the phrase and the body in three variants. Each time it asserts an "input text changed" error that names the right definition (`glossary.a` or `glossary.b`). It also asserts the record file is left unchanged.
- `changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required` asserts the exact diff lines. Only the changed body line appears, as a removal followed by an addition.
- `cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` also drops a definition input and asserts "glossary.b, found 0". It duplicates one and asserts "found 2".

**Moving an unchanged definition does not invalidate its snapshot**
`cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` prepends blank lines to `md/glossary.md`, which shifts every definition's position. It asserts that validation reports no errors.

**Evidence displays show name, current location, and recorded text**
`src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` records a definition input with text `recorded term`. It asserts the page contains `definition rules.term`, then the `rules.term` entry with its `md/rules.md` location and range, then the recorded text block. It also asserts the ordering within the "Referenced definitions" group.

**Residual notes**
- The "moving" test shifts definitions by inserting leading lines. It does not reorder two definitions within a chapter. A shift and a reorder both change location only, so I count this as the same input class.
- `schema_rejects_each_malformed_field_and_input_form` also exercises definition-input malformations. It is marked for `requirements.ci.schema`, not for this requirement. The marked tests already cover the obligations above, so I did not treat it as a gap.

No gaps found, and there are no acknowledgments to account for.
